questions.question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street, what should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: Why should you not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel at higher speeds than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop because of their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles take longer to stop than smaller vehicles. A sudden stop in front of them is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Your tires do not grip wet or icy roads as well as dry roads. Slow down when roads are wet or icy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand and arm signals because bicycles do not have turn signals. A left arm straight out means the bicyclist is turning left.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that traffic may be coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When driving in fog, which headlights should you use?
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and make visibility worse.

questions.question: You should never pass more than one vehicle at a time.
questions.explanation: Never pass more than one vehicle at a time. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your body. Coffee, food, or showers will not speed this up.

questions.question: You notice a driver ahead with one hand on the wheel talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that the driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.
Do not copy this driver's behavior.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted while driving by looking at passengers, searching your vehicle, reading, or daydreaming. If another driver seems distracted, give them extra space because they are more likely to cause an accident.

questions.question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn to catch your exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross the street illegally (not in a crosswalk), what must you do?

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.
Should honk your horn at them.

questions.explanation: You must always yield to pedestrians, even if they are crossing illegally or not in a crosswalk. You still must stop for them.

questions.question: In rain or fog, you should use which lights to see better?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, sleet, or fog. High beam headlights reflect off water and precipitation, making it harder to see.

questions.question: When may you pass another vehicle?

options.text: You are on a hill or curve.
You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.
You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
questions.explanation: A broken line means you can cross it to pass. A solid line means you cannot pass. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull over to the side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you about a steep hill ahead. Slow down to avoid brake damage or crashes.

questions.question: What does a 'No stopping' sign mean?

options.text: To avoid conflict with other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid conflict with other traffic.
questions.explanation: A 'No stopping' sign means you can only stop to obey a traffic signal, obey a police officer, or prevent a crash with another vehicle.

questions.question: You are angry after a work problem. When you get to your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly so you won't think about it.
Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
Stop at your favorite bar and have a few drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to cool off before you begin your drive home.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, take time to calm down before driving. Driving while emotional is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down, what should you do?

options.text: Signal and pull into the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.
Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard lights and get your vehicle off the road away from traffic as soon as possible. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: If you are in a serious car crash, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle off the road if possible. Check if anyone is hurt and call 911 if needed. Report the crash to police if there is injury, death, or more than $1,000 in damage.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop before you reach a school bus with flashing red lights. Stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a road with a median or center lane, vehicles on the opposite side do not need to stop.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: Fatigue makes you tired and slow to react. You may fall asleep while driving and crash, which can hurt or kill you or others.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A three-sided sign tells you to slow down at an intersection and be ready to stop. Let other drivers and pedestrians go first. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the right lane is ending. Cars in the right lane must move to the left lane.

questions.question: Distracted driving may be caused by:

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.
Changing a radio station or CD.

questions.explanation: Drivers make about 200 decisions for every mile they drive. You must focus completely on driving. Any other activity is dangerous.

questions.question: Orange is the color used for signs in construction work zones.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are usually orange and diamond-shaped or rectangular. Many are reflective so you can see them better at night.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Show them you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Stay calm and create distance between your car and theirs. Slow down and let them pass. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: If a truck or bus is turning right where you also need to turn right, you should:

options.text: Turn before the truck or bus does.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your car between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus has finished turning before you turn.

questions.question: To drive safely, you should make sure your physical condition does not affect your driving. You should:

options.text: Stay physically fit and have regular doctor visits.
Know how medicine affects your driving.
Only drive within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive if you can do so safely.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. You must stop:

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is lowered.
If the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if you see flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a stop sign, a flagger signaling you to stop, or a visible train. If you are not sure it is safe to cross, stop. Never try to race a train.
